statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is true if and only if the bitwise exclusive-or (XOR) of all n entries piles[0], ..., piles[n-1] is nonzero.
preconditions: Let n = len(piles). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 7, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= piles[i] <= 7.

statement: The function returns a result (some Bool); it does not fail by panic, integer overflow, or out-of-bounds access.
preconditions: Let n = len(piles). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 7, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= piles[i] <= 7.

statement: Whenever nim_game(piles) returns r and nim_game(q) returns rq, r = rq.
preconditions: Let n = len(piles). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 7; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= piles[i] <= 7; q is a sequence of length n; for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= q[i] <= 7; and q is a permutation of piles (for every integer v, the number of occurrences of v in q equals the number of occurrences of v in piles).

statement: Whenever nim_game(B) returns rB and nim_game(piles) returns rP, rB = rP.
preconditions: Let B be a sequence and x an integer. The preconditions are: 1 <= len(B) <= 5; for every k with 0 <= k < len(B), 1 <= B[k] <= 7; 1 <= x <= 7; and piles is the concatenation of B followed by two copies of x, so len(piles) = len(B) + 2.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r is true, there exists an index i with 0 <= i < n and an integer v with 0 <= v < piles[i] such that, letting updated be the sequence obtained from piles by replacing piles[i] with v, the XOR of all entries of updated is zero.
preconditions: Let n = len(piles). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 7, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= piles[i] <= 7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r and r is false, for every index i with 0 <= i < n and every integer v with 0 <= v < piles[i], letting updated be the sequence obtained from piles by replacing piles[i] with v, the XOR of all entries of updated is nonzero.
preconditions: Let n = len(piles). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 7, and for every i with 0 <= i < n, 1 <= piles[i] <= 7.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r is true.
preconditions: Let n = len(piles). The preconditions are: 1 <= n <= 7; for every k with 0 <= k < n, 1 <= piles[k] <= 7; and there exists an index i with 0 <= i < n such that piles[i] is strictly greater than the XOR of all entries piles[j] with j != i (the XOR of the empty set in the case n = 1 is 0).
